Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with viral upper respiratory tract infection presenting with 5–6 days of continuous dry cough, runny nose, subjective chills, muscle aches, fatigue, and transient mild diarrhea. High likelihood viral URI per clinical presentation and DDx.  
- DDx considers ACE inhibitor-induced cough as medium likelihood but unlikely primary cause due to acute onset with infective symptoms and long duration on medication.  
- Post-viral cough due to airway hyperreactivity considered medium likelihood; too early (5-6 days) to definitively label as post-viral.  
- Atypical bacterial infection (e.g., Mycoplasma pneumoniae) low to medium likelihood; lacks objective fever, chest signs, and sputum to support.  
- Diabetic-related immune compromise noted as possible contributing factor to prolonged illness and fatigue.  
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx; all DDx supported or consistent with clinical information.  

Management Plan  
- Symptomatic management advised: rest, adequate hydration, regular paracetamol for symptom relief  
- Monitor symptoms; return if no improvement within 2–3 days or if cough worsens, breathing difficulty develops, or fever persists  
- Recommend taking 1–2 days off work for rest due to cough and fatigue, then reassess fitness for return  
- Counsel regarding alcohol reduction due to blood pressure and diabetes control  
- No investigations or referrals currently indicated based on clinical picture

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
- Viral upper respiratory tract infection – High likelihood. Classical presentation with runny nose, dry cough, chills, muscle aches, and mild diarrhea at onset.  
- ACE inhibitor-induced cough – Medium likelihood. Fits dry cough profile but acute onset and infective symptoms argue against primary causation.  
- Post-viral cough due to airway hyperreactivity – Medium likelihood. Possible progression if cough persists beyond typical viral illness duration.  
- Atypical bacterial infection (e.g., Mycoplasma pneumoniae) – Low to medium likelihood. Some supporting symptoms but lacking systemic and respiratory signs.
